product_scope: Static analysis examined public Android XAPK artifacts for Foodvisor, MyFitnessPal, Cal AI, and YAZIO to look for manifest permissions, embedded runtime/model assets, endpoints, and strings related to food-photo inference.
supported_platforms: Android artifacts only; iOS binaries were not obtained or analyzed.
pricing: Not applicable to the static pass; consumer subscription information remains in the app-specific results.
popularity_signal: The four packages were selected as recognizable consumer nutrition/photo-calorie apps; selection is not a ranking or statistical market-share claim.
recognition_behavior: Static code confirms camera/photo-analysis UI and network-capable app boundaries. It does not reveal the complete runtime request/response behavior.
identified_services: [uncertain] Foodvisor exposes an api.foodvisor.io base URL. MFP, Cal AI, and YAZIO base APK inventories did not expose a named food-recognition vendor in the static strings searched; public product/privacy sources provide stronger provider clues for MFP and YAZIO.
model_or_provider_confidence: [uncertain] Absence of obvious model files is a weak negative signal. Models can be delivered from remote config, encrypted/obfuscated assets, split APKs, or native code.
local_inference_evidence: Foodvisor, MFP, Cal AI, and YAZIO XAPK trees had no obvious food model extensions (.tflite, .onnx, .mlmodel, .gguf, .mnn, .param, .pt, .pth, .lite, .ort). MFP and YAZIO contained ML Kit barcode models, not food models. This is compatible with server recognition or runtime model delivery.
portion_and_nutrition_method: Not determinable from static inventory alone.

static_findings: Foodvisor manifest: io.foodvisor.foodvisor, version 7.2.0, min SDK 28, target 35; CAMERA/INTERNET; api.foodvisor.io; ML Kit barcode classes. MFP: com.myfitnesspal.android, version 26.27.0, min SDK 32, target 36; CAMERA/INTERNET; bundled barcode TFLite models. Cal AI: com.viraldevelopment.calai, version 26.28.0, min SDK 29, target 36; CAMERA/INTERNET; obfuscated assets; ML Kit barcode/remote-model infrastructure. YAZIO: com.yazio.android, version 26.29.0, min SDK 32, target 35; CAMERA/INTERNET; AI food-tracking resources; bundled barcode TFLite models. JADX was used on the base APKs; Foodvisor and YAZIO produced readable decompiled trees, while large MFP/Cal AI trees were partially decompiled before the long-running jobs were stopped after static evidence was collected.
reverse_engineering_limits: Only publicly downloadable artifacts were used. Nothing was installed or executed; no paid account, DRM bypass, authentication bypass, network interception, or redistribution of decompiled code was attempted. Publisher terms may restrict reverse engineering. Static analysis cannot prove current production behavior.
candidate_models: No bundled food model was identified. A new app should explicitly control model assets, versioning, checksums, rollback, and runtime download policy instead of relying on accidental binary discovery.
mobile_runtime_support: APK evidence shows ordinary Android camera/ML Kit plumbing, not a complete embedded food VLM. For SuperNutrition evaluate LiteRT, ONNX Runtime Mobile, ExecuTorch, and Core ML separately.
device_requirements: No inference benchmark was run. Package size and permission inventories are not substitutes for peak RAM, latency, battery, or thermal measurements.
expected_food_inference_quality: Not inferable from static artifacts; public product help pages and benchmark literature indicate common visible foods are easier than mixed meals and portions.
unit_cost_estimate: No per-photo API cost can be inferred from an APK. Network endpoints may be first-party or vendor-backed and may use private contracts.
privacy_and_compliance: Permissions and endpoints show camera/network capability, not retention. Verify privacy policies, App Store/Data Safety labels, and traffic contracts separately.
recommendation: Use static analysis as corroboration only. For a definitive current provider/runtime answer, obtain written vendor disclosures or perform an authorized, consented runtime test of an app account; do not treat decompiled strings as proof of active execution.
